content:
I mentioned in my Siri AI Apple Watch article today that there's still one change I hope Apple can add before watchOS 27 launches at the end of the month. This is a feature that's been around for years and has become muscle memory — I've found it really inconvenient all summer.

In watchOS 27, double-clicking the Digital Crown can no longer quickly switch between different apps

I wrote about this earlier this morning:

I first raised this issue back in July when they released the first public beta of watchOS 27, and I had already passed my feedback along to Apple in June.

For years, Apple Watch has had a hidden gesture built in that lets you quickly switch between two apps, or between the last app you used and the watch face.

It's an action I haven't thought about consciously in years, but I've been using it the whole time.

In watchOS 27, both single-press and double-press of the Digital Crown bring up the dynamic App Grid

The first beta of watchOS 27 removed this feature. It looks like Apple wanted to heavily promote the newly launched "dynamic App Grid" in watchOS 27. Now pressing the Digital Crown shows the Siri app icon, plus five smart-recommended app icons, plus another icon for viewing the full App Grid.

The dynamic App Grid is actually getting more pleasant to use the more I try it. If the app you're looking for is already in the smart suggestions row, it's genuinely handy.

But it still can't replace the reliable, snappy feel of double-clicking the Digital Crown to jump between apps. In watchOS 27, that's completely impossible. In the watchOS 27 beta, double-clicking the Digital Crown does exactly the same thing as single-clicking it.

The old method let you bounce between apps like Workout and Music in a flash.

As I mentioned before, Apple Watch has extremely few physical buttons — only the Ultra model has an Action button. Given that, I think dropping the double-click gesture on one of those buttons is a real mistake.

Double-clicking the side button below the Digital Crown is still there: it brings up your Apple Wallet cards. Hopefully the final release of watchOS 27 can bring back the same gesture on the Digital Crown, or at least add it back in watchOS 27.1.

Do you use this gesture normally? Does it feel inconvenient to you in the watchOS 27 beta? Will you miss it once you update? Drop a comment and let me know.
